name: Duskline Banded Collar Shirt
description:
A clean, relaxed banded-collar shirt cut from a medium-weight cotton-modal blend in a deep indigo that fades slightly at the seams — intentional, not wear. The collar sits close without choking, the placket runs four buttons down, and the hem is cut slightly longer in the back for tucking or leaving out. Sleeves can be rolled and stayed with a small interior button tab. It breathes well, drapes well, and looks equally at home in a Tier 3 apartment kitchen or a mid-range restaurant.

Favored by people who want to look put-together without looking like they're trying. The Duskline shirt has been in continuous production by Veramar Goods for over a decade with minimal changes — the kind of product that stays in the catalog because it simply works. You see it on schoolteachers, freelance architects, and the occasional off-duty transit cop.
what_it_says: I have taste and I don't need to prove it.
story_hooks: A character finds one still in its original packaging inside a derelict Tier 3 apartment — the previous tenant left in a hurry and never came back.
Veramar Goods has been quietly bought out by a corponation; the next production run will carry a corporate wellness logo on the hem. The old stock is quietly becoming collectible.
Someone wearing this shirt is found dead in a Tier 1 access corridor — the shirt is clean, pristine, and completely out of place.
